newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip on profit-taking after US data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip on profit-taking after US data.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds eased on profit-taking after last week's rise, despite market-friendly U.S. May CPI data which supported the belief U.S. interest rates are unlikely to rise, dealers said on Tuesday.
MinFins, like other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news which would suggest a change in U.S. interest rates and consequently affect U.S. Treasury bond prices.
"A correction started after the figures although these were not bad for us," an International Moscow Bank dealer said. "The market is lower and profit-taking looks like the main reason."
Avtobank dealer Ivan Kuznetsov said the MinFin market had been otherwise calm over the day .
Dealers said Western banks were seen selling, apparently on client offer while Russian banks were mostly bidding.
